record.paper_title: Problems in Data Structures and Algorithms
record.original_question: For the minimum spanning tree problem in a connected undirected graph with m edges and n vertices, is random sampling actually necessary in order to obtain linear running time? Equivalently, does there exist a deterministic linear-time algorithm for computing a minimum spanning tree?

evidence.quote: One may ask whether random sampling is really necessary. Is there a deterministic linear-time algorithm to find minimum spanning trees?

In conclusion, we now know that minimum spanning trees can be found in linear time using random sampling, and we know an optimum deterministic algorithm but we don’t know how fast it runs (no slower than O(m α(n)), possibly as fast as O(m)).

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a deterministic linear-time MST algorithm in the comparison-based model is widely cited as still open. The best known deterministic comparison-based bound remains Chazelle's O(m α(m,n)), and Pettie–Ramachandran give an algorithm of provably optimal (but unknown explicit) running time. No deterministic O(m+n) algorithm has been reported as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: An Optimal Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithm (Pettie & Ramachandran)
status_evidence.snippet: deterministic algorithm whose running time is provably optimal... the exact function describing it is not known at present
status_evidence.claim: The Pettie–Ramachandran deterministic algorithm is optimal in an abstract sense, but its actual running time is not known, leaving the deterministic linear-time MST question open.
